hero.headline: Rapids Water Park hosts Adults Night and free dad admission during Father's Day weekend in Riviera Beach
hero.teaser: Rapids Water Park in Riviera Beach offers special events this summer including glow-filled Adults Night for guests 21 and older and free admission for dads June 20-21.
hero.body:
Rapids Water Park is making waves this summer with a mix of special events aimed at all ages. Elliott Russell, director of marketing and sales, told WPTV that Adults Night returns with music, glow items, and exclusive park access for guests 21 and older. The event is being billed as a chance for grown-ups to enjoy the slides, lazy river, and wave pool under the stars.

Greg Fuller, the park's general manager, said families can also take advantage of free admission for dads on June 20-21. On June 25, Rapids will join Live Like Jake and other participants worldwide for the World's Largest Swim Lesson, a coordinated effort to raise awareness about water safety.

The park, located at 6566 N. Military Trail in Riviera Beach, is open daily with various ticket packages. New viral treats including specialty funnel cakes are making an appearance this season.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Teen Killed in Shooting After Instagram Firearm Exchange
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce teenager died in a shooting following an alleged firearm exchange arranged on Instagram.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce teen was killed in a shooting that authorities say followed a planned firearm exchange arranged through Instagram. The incident occurred recently in Fort Pierce.

Police are investigating the shooting as part of an alleged gun transaction coordinated on social media. The teen was fatally shot during the encounter.

Authorities described the case as unusual. Law enforcement is continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the Instagram-arranged firearm exchange and the fatal shooting.

cards.headline: Planned Gun Exchange Led to Fatal Fort Pierce Bicycle Shooting
cards.teaser: A planned gun exchange resulted in a bicycle shooting that killed a teenager in Fort Pierce, according to police.
cards.body:
A teenager riding a bicycle in Fort Pierce was shot and killed during what police say was a planned gun exchange. Fort Pierce police are investigating the fatal shooting.

The shooting occurred after the gun exchange was arranged. The teen was on a bicycle when the fatal incident took place.

Police say the gun exchange was planned prior to the shooting. Investigators are working to determine all the circumstances surrounding the fatal encounter in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Indian River County sewage system getting $1 million federal grant for Ixora Park upgrade
cards.teaser: A $1 million federal grant will help fund a major sewage system upgrade in Indian River County affecting over 230 homes in the Ixora Park community.
cards.body:
A $1 million federal grant will help fund a major sewage system upgrade in Indian River County, Congressman Mike Haridopolos announced at an afternoon press conference Wednesday. The Member Community Project Funding will support a $20.8 million project to retrofit the sewage system in the Ixora Park community, affecting over 230 homes that currently rely on a failing sewer system risking contamination of environmental resources. Haridopolos said the federal support ensures health and safety to the community by rehabilitating infrastructure while protecting the Indian River Lagoon, a designated federal resource and one of the most diverse estuaries in the country.

The Ixora Park community sits adjacent to the County South Relief Canal, which discharges into the Indian River Lagoon. Keith Drewett of the Clean Water Coalition of Indian River County said the lagoon is dramatically different from twenty years ago in terms of fishing and swimming, with nobody swimming in the lagoon anymore. Drewett attributed the environmental challenges to the high water table and heavy rainfall flowing underground through the subsurface. The project will replace aging sewer infrastructure to protect water quality by reducing discharges of nitrogen and phosphorus into the lagoon. Haridopolos said the benefits extend beyond environmental protection, noting that replacing the infrastructure improves both water quality and the taxable value of homes in the area.

hero.headline: Jupiter approves fire assessment fee to fund new fire rescue department starting October 1
hero.teaser: Jupiter's town council approved a fire assessment fee to help fund the town's new fire rescue department, which begins service Oct. 1. The fee will cover about 8 percent of the total department cost.
hero.body:
Jupiter's town council has approved a fire assessment fee designed to help finance the town's new fire rescue department, which will launch on October 1. The per-property charge will contribute approximately 8 percent of the department's total operating costs. Property taxes will cover 84 percent of expenses, while the remaining 8 percent will come from EMS transport fees. The new assessment replaces the current county fire fee that residents see on their tax bills.

Finance Director Scott Reynolds emphasized that the funding structure will deliver meaningful financial relief to property owners, a goal the town has pursued for three years. "The immediate savings for property owners, we've been talking about this for three years, starting at $25 million so right out of the gate, a $10 million savings to the residents," Reynolds said. To help residents understand their individual situation, the town has created an online calculator where people can estimate their potential savings under the new system.

Mayor Jim Kuretski cast the only vote against the funding structure, expressing concerns about inconsistencies in how the assessment applies to different property types. Single family homes are assessed based on total square footage, including garages and porches, while townhomes and condos are assessed differently. This discrepancy prompted Kuretski to question the fairness of the calculation method across the community.

The town mailed information letters about the fee to 30,000 homes, though Town of Jupiter spokesperson Mariana DiNunzio acknowledged the change has caused some confusion among residents. "I think there's been some confusion because it's new. The town hasn't had to have this, a non ad-valorem assessment," DiNunzio said. Some residents have also expressed concerns about the fee's potential to increase in the future, questioning what might happen as time passes. The town's online calculator provides residents with a tool to better understand how the new assessment will affect their individual properties and to see what financial benefits they can expect from the transition to a municipal fire rescue department.

cards.headline: Public safety spending drives property tax debate in Palm Beach County
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County Administrator Joe Abruzzo confronted state Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia over property tax cuts, with spending on public safety becoming the main point of contention.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County Administrator Joe Abruzzo confronted state Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia this week over property tax cuts, with public safety spending emerging as a central dispute. Abruzzo explained that most taxpayer dollars collected in the county fund public safety, including $1.1 billion for the sheriff and approximately $700 million for fire rescue. When all county departments are calculated, only $609 million remains after removing first responders, Abruzzo said Tuesday. "The $609 million is what he is essentially attacking," Abruzzo said of Ingoglia's position.

Ingoglia announced in Boca Raton that Palm Beach County was overspending by $443 million, supporting a fall referendum to raise the Homestead Exemption to $250,000 in 2027 and $500,000 in 2028. Abruzzo invited Ingoglia to review the budget, noting that this year's new revenue of approximately $73 million is already being absorbed by the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. The sheriff is requesting a $94 million increase, roughly $20 million more than the county is receiving in extra money from new properties this year, Abruzzo said. The Palm Beach Sheriff's Office responded that ensuring citizen safety is government's most important function. Former Florida State Senator Jeff Brandes suggested sheriff's offices and police departments may need alternative funding sources if tax reform passes.

cards.headline: Lake Worth Beach commission approves 10-year lease extension for Benny's on the Beach through 2043
cards.teaser: The Lake Worth Beach City Commission unanimously approved a 10-year lease extension for Benny's on the Beach, pushing the pier restaurant's lease from January 2033 to February 2043 with a 5 percent rent increase every two years.
cards.body:
The Lake Worth Beach City Commission unanimously approved a 10-year lease extension for Benny's on the Beach, extending the pier restaurant's lease from January 2033 to February 2043 with a 5 percent rent increase every two years. The decision followed public debate over fairness, community benefit, and the timing of the extension, which comes seven years before the current agreement expires. City staff noted that Benny's had requested the maximum 30-year term allowed under city rules. Owner Dylan Lipton defended the extension by highlighting the restaurant's four-decade presence in the community, its employment of more than 100 local residents, its $1 million annual investment in maintenance and repairs, and its role as a major tourism driver.

Opposition came from multiple residents. Jenny Powell questioned the timing and resident benefits, while Kim Stokes raised concerns about unequal treatment compared to the Beach Club. Nancy Udell warned against limiting future commissions' options. Commissioner Christopher Serafinchan led advocacy for the extension, calling Benny's the city's highest-paying tenant and cautioning that rejecting it could bring higher-priced replacements. Commissioner Sarah Malega conducted an affordability check, finding a $16 breakfast before tip. Commissioners Mimi May and Mayor Betty Resch cited Benny's community involvement and property investment as reasons for support. The commission approved the extension unanimously.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach residents fight to save 10-acre forest from 72-townhome development
cards.teaser: Boynton Beach residents are continuing their fight to preserve a nearly 10-acre forest along city and county lines, pushing back against a developer's proposal to build 72 townhomes near Quentin Avenue and Nickels Blvd.
cards.body:
Boynton Beach residents are continuing their fight to preserve a nearly 10-acre forest along city and county lines, pushing back against a developer's proposal to build 72 townhomes near their neighborhood. The land sits near Quentin Avenue and Nickels Boulevard, where a boundary line separates two adjoining parcels home to gopher tortoises, grey foxes and other wildlife. Michael Zwierzyna, who has lived in the neighborhood since 2020, said the forest has become part of his family's daily routine. "Being able to have this local to your house is great," Zwierzyna said. "My children love being able to see a tortoise."

Developers with Mizner Global purchased nearly 10 acres of county land in March 2025 and also sought to purchase the city's portion of Nickels Forest for $5 million, a move the city halted. The revised proposal now calls for 72 townhomes, up from an earlier plan for 34 single-family homes. During Tuesday's city commission meeting, city leaders agreed to discuss the item at a later meeting. Commissioner Thomas Turkin voiced support for preservation, saying the city's land should be preserved. Residents have raised concerns about stop work order signs posted on the property, pointing to trees they say were disturbed without proper permits. The group's petition on Change.org has gathered more than 1,500 signatures.

cards.headline: Jupiter beach dance parties to continue at sea turtle nesting area with new lighting rules
cards.teaser: Weekend beach dance parties will continue at Jupiter's sea turtle nesting area with lighting adjustments following a meeting of local, county, and state stakeholders with Loggerhead Marinelife Center.
cards.body:
Weekend beach dance parties will continue at Jupiter's sea turtle nesting area with lighting adjustments. The Town of Jupiter held a meeting Wednesday afternoon at the police department, bringing together local, county, and state stakeholders along with representatives from Loggerhead Marinelife Center to address concerns about the weekend beach dance parties held in the nesting area. The meeting lasted about an hour and a half.

Representatives from the dance group said the gathering was productive and that the parties will continue with some adjustments. "We're going to continue, just a couple of adjustments. Beautiful," Foreli of Happy Beach Dancing said. The adjustments will focus on reducing the amount of lighting used during the events to avoid disturbing nesting sea turtles. There had been calls from some to move the dancing away from the area entirely during nesting season. The group said they will be at Beach Access 55 again this Saturday.

cards.headline: Jupiter surgeon uses opioid-free protocol for joint replacement patients at Jupiter Medical Center
cards.teaser: Andrew Noble, an orthopedic surgeon at Jupiter Medical Center, is using the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery protocol to help patients recover from joint replacement surgery without ever touching an opioid.
cards.body:
Andrew Noble, an orthopedic surgeon at Jupiter Medical Center, is taking a different approach to joint replacement surgery built on the idea that patients who never receive pills they don't need are never put at risk in the first place. Noble uses the Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol combined with his own proprietary method to help patients recover from joint replacement surgery without ever touching an opioid. "Instead of chasing pain, it's a way of trying to stay ahead of pain, and have less pain afterwards with less need for opioids," Noble said. The ERAS protocol combines robotics for minimally invasive surgery, targeted numbing, and a timed schedule of non-opioid medications taken before, during, and after surgery.

Patient April Stubbs recovered from knee replacement surgery without opioids using this approach. "I never had to touch the more serious pain medications. The opioids, never even had to take any," Stubbs said. At Reprieve Recovery in Jupiter, Chief Marketing Officer Daniel Warren said patients are often unaware of the physical effects of opioid medications taken during surgical recovery. Warren noted that patients may experience withdrawal symptoms after taking opioids for two weeks without understanding why. "If a physician's able to provide recovery time or recovery medication regimen that exposes the patient to a lot less risk of developing a substance use disorder, then that's definitely a step in the right direction," Warren said.

hero.headline: West Palm Beach woman charged with posing as parking official in $1 scam on Worth Avenue
hero.teaser: Palm Beach police arrested a 19-year-old who allegedly impersonated a parking official and targeted drivers with a $1 parking scam, stealing credit card information from visitors.
hero.body:
Palm Beach police arrested Ti'Miyah De'Asia Allen, 19, of West Palm Beach, after she allegedly posed as a parking official and defrauded drivers on Worth Avenue. Investigators say Allen impersonated an employee of ParkMobile and the Palm Beach Parking Authority while targeting unsuspecting visitors and stealing their credit card information.

According to the arrest affidavit, Allen used a common approach to carry out the scheme. She would tell drivers looking to pay for parking that they could pay her approximately $1 instead of the standard $5 per hour plus a 40-cent transaction fee. To make the scam appear legitimate, she carried what looked like a ParkMobile payment device and displayed a fake badge. She would approach vehicles either before drivers had paid for parking or while they were in the process of paying. One victim reported that a fraudulent charge of $2,500 to a company called Health Aid appeared on their credit card after an interaction with Allen on June 5. Police noted that the town was "deprived of parking fee revenue that would have otherwise been legitimately paid."

The investigation revealed that elderly residents were specifically targeted in the scheme. Police say all of the victims were over 65 years old, making them particularly vulnerable to the fraud. This pattern of targeting seniors raised additional concerns for investigators about the nature and scope of the criminal activity.

Allen's arrest history suggests this was not her first fraudulent scheme. Police say she was involved in a similar operation last year while employed at a Wawa location on Belvedere Road, where she allegedly voided customer transactions for profit. Based on the evidence gathered in the current investigation, Allen has been charged with three crimes: falsely impersonating an officer, organized scheme to defraud, and unlawful use of a badge or other indicia of authority. The multiple charges reflect the coordinated nature of the scheme and the deliberate use of fake credentials to carry out the fraud.

hero.headline: Promise Fund to offer free mammogram screenings in Jupiter and West Palm Beach next month
hero.teaser: Women in Palm Beach County will have two opportunities in July to receive free mammogram screenings through events hosted by Promise Fund, a South Florida nonprofit focused on increasing survivorship from breast and cervical cancer.
hero.body:
Women in Palm Beach County will have two chances next month to get free mammogram screenings through Promise Fund, a South Florida nonprofit dedicated to improving breast and cervical cancer survival rates. The organization is hosting free mammography screening events on July 11 in Jupiter and July 12 in West Palm Beach. These screenings are made possible through partnerships with Florida Mobile Mammography, HealthyMe, the Health Care District of Palm Beach County, Origin Church, the Florida Department of Health and Monarch Health Services.

The Jupiter screening takes place July 11 starting at 8 a.m. on Indiantown Road, while the West Palm Beach event is scheduled for July 12 beginning at 9 a.m. Both events require advance appointments. Women interested in participating can register by calling 877-427-7664. The screenings are designed to reach women who might not otherwise have access to mammography services.

According to Lissette Lahoz, Promise Fund's Palm Beach County navigator, the organization works to remove barriers to healthcare access. "The Promise Fund is here to make screenings accessible for everyone, especially those who might otherwise go without care," Lahoz said. She emphasized the importance of early detection, noting that "Early detection can make a real difference. Treatment is often easier to manage, and people are able to focus more on their health, their families, and their everyday lives."

Promise Fund serves uninsured, underinsured and underserved women throughout Palm Beach, Broward and Martin counties. The nonprofit has reached more than 145,000 women across South Florida through education and outreach initiatives. To date, more than 27,000 women have accessed screenings, diagnostic services and care through the organization's programs. Additionally, 286 women who received cancer diagnoses have gotten assistance navigating their treatment. Promise Fund currently operates four co-located screening programs across Palm Beach and Broward counties and is working to secure funding to expand services into Martin County.

cards.headline: Portugal fans pack Loxahatchee club to watch World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Dozens of Portugal supporters packed the Portuguese American Culture Society of Palm Beach County in Loxahatchee Wednesday to watch Portugal's opening World Cup.
cards.body:
Dozens of Portugal supporters gathered at the Portuguese American Culture Society of Palm Beach County in Loxahatchee to watch Portugal's opening World Cup match, surrounded by Portuguese beer, wine, and food from the Iberian Peninsula. Vic Piorro, treasurer of the club, said the energy in the room reflected how deeply soccer is woven into Portuguese identity. "In Portugal, you have soccer, that's all there is. So it's very much part of our culture and our tradition," Piorro said. The club has served as a gathering place for the local Portuguese community since 1981.

Among the fans in attendance were Jonathan Reinoso and his father, Johnny-Lee Reinoso, who left work early to attend. Jonathan has been a superfan since childhood. When the Portuguese national team established a practice facility in Palm Beach Gardens, his father arranged for Jonathan to meet the team, including Cristiano Ronaldo. "I've been a fan my whole life, and when I just met him, it was just a dream, like I was in complete shock," Jonathan said. Though the game ended in a tie, the night remained a celebration for the Reinoso family and other supporters at the club. "It just means like so much to me. It's just like my whole heart. I love it," Jonathan said.

cards.headline: Floridians say $1 gas price increase would tank summer road trips
cards.teaser: Two out of three Floridians say higher prices could tank their summer road trips this year, according to a new survey showing drivers would cancel plans if gas prices rise another $1.01.
cards.body:
A new survey by RV Windshield Replacement shows that two out of three Floridians say higher gas prices could "tank" their summer road trips this year. WPTV Anchor Hollani Davis spoke with drivers at a gas station on 45th Street in West Palm Beach about whether they could afford increased travel costs. Florida drivers polled in the survey say if gas prices go up another $1.01, their summer road trip travel would be off. "No. There is no way," one driver told Davis. "I mean, no one can unless you're rich," said another driver WPTV connected with.

The survey found that 68% of Florida drivers agree shorter state trips might be most doable, but some say even that could be tough to pull off. One WPTV viewer who travels to Orlando explained the impact on their travel frequency: "For me, going to Orlando sometimes, I'm thinking instead of going every two weeks, I go like once a month, or even sometimes I skip a month because of the gas price." Gas prices are starting to fall just in time as the summer travel season begins.

hero.headline: Rapids Water Park hosts Adults Night and free dad admission during Father's Day weekend in Riviera Beach
hero.teaser: Rapids Water Park in Riviera Beach offers special events this summer including glow-filled Adults Night for guests 21 and older and free admission for dads June 20-21.
hero.body:
Rapids Water Park is making waves this summer with a mix of special events aimed at all ages. Elliott Russell, director of marketing and sales, told WPTV that Adults Night returns with music, glow items, and exclusive park access for guests 21 and older. The event is being billed as a chance for grown-ups to enjoy the slides, lazy river, and wave pool under the stars.

Greg Fuller, the park's general manager, said families can also take advantage of free admission for dads on June 20-21. On June 25, Rapids will join Live Like Jake and other participants worldwide for the World's Largest Swim Lesson, a coordinated effort to raise awareness about water safety.

The park, located at 6566 N. Military Trail in Riviera Beach, is open daily with various ticket packages. New viral treats including specialty funnel cakes are making an appearance this season.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Library launches summer reading challenge with prizes and events through July 31
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Library System invites readers of all ages to participate in its 2026 Summer Reading Challenge, offering free activities, incentives and grand prizes.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Library System is inviting readers of all ages to "Unearth a Story" this summer as part of its 2026 Summer Reading Challenge, running through July 31. Community Engagement Manager Lindsey McMullen told WPTV the program offers free activities, incentives and grand prizes to encourage residents to rediscover the joy of reading. Participants can register at any library branch, complete an activity log and return it to claim a prize while supplies last. Returned logs also qualify readers for a drawing to win one of several grand prizes.

Little learners up to age 4 can take home a fun rubber duck, while kids ages 5 to 11 can choose from a fidget spinner, dinosaur-themed pop keychain or dino pencil. Teens ages 12 to 17 and adults can opt for a fidget spinner, chip clip or notebook. Each branch is hosting special events including children's story times, craft sessions, adult workshops and wellness programs. Families will see Dewey the Library Owl and Penelope Rex, a dinosaur character, at various appearances throughout the challenge. According to the American Library Association, summertime reading programs help prevent the "summer slide" in student learning.

cards.headline: Smithsonian Marine Exhibit in Fort Pierce showcases Florida ocean ecosystems with live displays
cards.body:
The Smithsonian Marine Ecosystems Exhibit at the St. Lucie County Aquarium invites visitors to explore Florida's coastal habitats through live encounters with marine life at 420 Seaway Drive in Fort Pierce. Manager Bill Hoffman told WPTV that the facility's philosophy of displaying fully live, complex models of ecosystems dates back to 1980 under the Smithsonian, setting it apart from typical public aquariums. "We feel like we're the best kept secret on the Treasure Coast, and we don't want to be," Hoffman said, noting that the facility houses more species than many larger exhibits. The centerpiece is the Atlantic coral reef tank, which recreates one of Florida's most significant coastal ecosystems. Visitors also encounter live models of seagrass beds, mangroves, and hardbottom communities that demonstrate intricate relationships between organisms, including a four-inch barracuda.

The exhibit operates as a partnership between the St. Lucie County Aquarium and the Smithsonian Marine Station to raise public awareness about ocean threats while inspiring conservation efforts. A touch tank allows guests to handle unusual marine species under staff supervision, where exhibit educator Chelsie Corcoran notes visitors often encounter animals they have never seen before. The facility plans upcoming programming to coincide with its 25th anniversary celebration later this year. The exhibit is open to the public year-round, with more information available at sms.si.edu and on the Smithsonian Marine Station's social media channels.

hero.headline: Florida Professional Firefighters Endorse Ashley Moody for U.S. Senate
hero.body:
The Florida Professional Firefighters union has thrown its support behind U.S. Senator Ashley Moody as she runs for election this November. The statewide organization previously backed Moody during her 2022 reelection campaign for Florida Attorney General and is now endorsing her Senate bid. Governor Ron DeSantis appointed Moody to fill a U.S. Senate vacancy last year.

FPF President Wayne "Bernie" Bernoska praised Moody's track record of supporting firefighters and paramedics throughout her public service career. "Senator Ashley Moody has been a steadfast supporter of Florida's firefighters and paramedics throughout her career in public service," Bernoska said. He noted her commitment to public safety has remained consistent from her time as Florida Attorney General through her current Senate service, highlighting her dedication to the men and women who respond to emergencies daily.

Moody expressed gratitude for the endorsement and reaffirmed her commitment to first responders. "Our firefighters run toward danger so the rest of us can run to safety, and for over 80 years, the Florida Professional Firefighters organization has represented that brotherhood with distinction. To have their trust is a recognition from a family I am proud to be part of," she said. Moody emphasized that firefighters and paramedics who risk their lives deserve a senator actively fighting for their interests and those of their families.

The union highlighted specific legislative efforts demonstrating Moody's support for first responders. Moody introduced the Homes for Every Local Protector, Educator, and Responder Act, known as the HELPER Act and designated as S 978. This proposed legislation would create a Federal Housing Administration program designed to provide mortgage assistance to first responders, including firefighters, as well as teachers. The firefighters' association pointed to this work as evidence of Moody's concrete commitment to improving the lives of public safety professionals and educators across Florida. The endorsement signals the union's confidence that Moody will continue advocating for firefighters' interests as an elected senator representing the state.

cards.headline: Florida Attorney General Reaffirms Parental Authority Over Religious Education Programs
cards.teaser: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier issued an opinion supporting release time religious instruction programs, affirming that parents hold primary responsibility for directing the education and religious upbringing of their children.
cards.body:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier reaffirmed parental authority over children's religious education in a recent opinion addressing release time religious instruction programs. Responding to a question raised by Senator Clay Yarborough, Uthmeier concluded that when parents choose to add religious instruction as part of their child's education, public schools must respect and accommodate that decision. The opinion was directed to school districts across Florida and recognizes a foundational American principle: parents, not government, bear the primary responsibility for directing the education and religious upbringing of their children.

The opinion references more than a century of U.S. Supreme Court precedent establishing parental authority. In Society of Sisters, the Court declared that "the child is not the mere creature of the State." Wisconsin v. Yoder protected parents' ability to direct their children's religious education from government interference, and Mahmoud v. Taylor recognized that parents retain primary responsibility for their children's upbringing, especially regarding matters of faith and conscience. Release time religious instruction programs allow students to leave campus during part of the school day to receive religious instruction off school property with parental permission. The Supreme Court upheld such programs more than 70 years ago in Zorach v. Clauson. Uthmeier's opinion states that school districts cannot frustrate parental decisions simply because administrators prefer a different approach.

cards.headline: Alachua County Sets Ballot for Commission and School Board Races
cards.teaser: Florida's candidate qualifying deadline has passed, finalizing the ballot for several local Alachua County elections. The county, home to Gainesville and the University of Florida, was one of five counties in Florida that Democrat Charlie Crist carried in his 2022 gubernatorial campaign.
cards.body:
The County Commission District 2 seat is open after incumbent Marihelen Wheeler announced she would not seek a third term. Four Democrats have qualified: Donna Bradbrook, Tina Certain, Charlie Jackson and Byran Williams. Republican Robert Woody withdrew his candidacy. With only Democrats on the ballot, the August 18 contest will be a Universal Primary open to all voters regardless of party and will decide the race. Certain currently serves as the District 1 School Board member and is leaving her seat to run for Commission. Bradbrook has raised $26,905 through the latest reporting period, including $25,000 of her own funds. Certain has raised $17,115 with over 200 individual donors and a $150 contribution from her school board colleague Sarah Rockwell. Jackson has raised $8,520, and Williams reports $2,349.

In County Commission District 4, Democratic incumbent Ken Cornell is running for a fourth term and has raised $107,000. His opponent, no-party candidate Dewayne Baines, is a social worker, teacher and Christian counselor who has raised $700. Republican Van Elmore withdrew his candidacy on June 10 after failing to raise sufficient funds to pay the candidate qualifying fee.

cards.headline: Democratic Recruiter June Piscitelli Endorses Amanda Marie Green in Florida Congressional District 2
cards.teaser: Amanda Marie Green added June Piscitelli to her endorsement list. Piscitelli has spent decades helping women run for and win public office and now serves as Chair for Ruth's List Florida.
cards.body:
Amanda Marie Green announced the endorsement of June Piscitelli, a longtime recruiter and mentor of pro-choice Democratic women candidates. Piscitelli currently serves as Chair for Ruth's List Florida, a network dedicated to expanding women's representation at every level of government. "Amanda impressed me from the moment I met her," Piscitelli said. "She is an honest, trustworthy, and intelligent woman. Her integrity is needed in Washington, and she has the skills and abilities to make D.C., and Florida, a better space." Green, a former international development professional who spent a decade managing taxpayer-funded programs and delivering services around the world, is running on lowering costs for working families, supporting North Florida's agricultural economy, protecting health care access, and restoring accountability in Washington.

Green faces a contested Democratic Primary on August 18 for the seat Neal Dunn is leaving open. Green said Piscitelli's work has opened doors for countless women across Florida and that her endorsement is important because she understands the need for leaders focused on solving problems, delivering results for their communities, and protecting fundamental freedoms for women. The Piscitelli endorsement joins a growing coalition backing Green's campaign that includes former U.S. Representative Allen Boyd and the Florida AFL-CIO. Her full and growing list of endorsements is posted on her campaign website.

cards.headline: Poll Analyst Calls New Congressional Survey in Florida 'Heavily Salted'
cards.teaser: Political analyst Steve Vancore applied his Salt Shaker test to a new Change Research poll showing David Jolly leading Byron Donalds 47% to 42% in the 2026 congressional race, warning the survey deserves a generous pour of Morton's salt.
cards.body:
A new Change Research poll showing David Jolly leading Byron Donalds 47% to 42% in the 2026 congressional race warrants significant scrutiny, according to poll analyst Steve Vancore. While the poll demonstrates transparency by disclosing its client, recruitment sources, weighting variables, post-stratification targets and limitations, and employs reasonable sample sizes with appropriate weighting on age, gender, race, education, 2024 Presidential vote and region, several methodological problems undermine its reliability.

The survey's opt-in sample, including recruitment through Facebook and Instagram ads, risks overrepresenting voters motivated enough to respond during a period of high Democratic enthusiasm. Conducting the survey only in English presents a serious limitation in a state with substantial Spanish-dominant Hispanic communities. Additionally, the poll included self-described likely voters despite 20% of respondents saying they were not likely to vote. Most problematically, the ballot test presented voters with descriptions and photos of both candidates rather than asking a clean, uninformed question. Jolly received more favorable framing and more words, while Donalds' description emphasized endorsements, corporate ties and combative language. Vancore concluded the poll should not be dismissed outright given its relative transparency compared to most surveys, but the combination of opt-in recruiting, English-only fielding, self-described voter behavior and narrative ballot testing all point toward taking these findings with substantial skepticism.

cards.headline: Former Florida Senate President Bill Galvano Speaks at Flagler Tiger Bay Club
cards.teaser: Former Florida Senate President Bill Galvano reflected on Florida's successes and challenges during a presentation at the Flagler Tiger Bay Club.
cards.body:
Galvano, who previously served as President of the Florida Senate, addressed the Flagler Tiger Bay Club on topics related to the state's achievements and ongoing challenges. The event was reported by Flagler News Weekly.

The Flagler Tiger Bay Club hosts regular speakers and forums on political and civic issues affecting Florida and the nation. The organization provides a nonpartisan platform for discussion of public policy matters.

hero.headline: Fire breaks out on roof of Dillard's store at Treasure Coast Square Mall in Jensen Beach
hero.body:
Multiple Martin County Fire Rescue units battled a roof fire at the Dillard's department store in Jensen Beach Wednesday night. The call came in just before 9 p.m. at Treasure Coast Square Mall.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the fire appears to have started on the west side of the mall near Dillard's. Investigators believe the fire was caused by possible electrical issues or lightning.

Firefighters worked to extinguish the flames on the roof of the department store. Residents were asked to avoid the area while crews responded to the scene.

The incident remained under investigation as of late Wednesday evening. Martin County Fire Rescue had multiple units on scene working to control the blaze.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Teen Killed in Shooting After Instagram Firearm Exchange
hero.teaser: A Fort Pierce teenager died in a shooting following an alleged firearm exchange arranged on Instagram.
hero.body:
A Fort Pierce teen was killed in a shooting that authorities say followed a planned firearm exchange arranged through Instagram. The incident occurred recently in Fort Pierce.

Police are investigating the shooting as part of an alleged gun transaction coordinated on social media. The teen was fatally shot during the encounter.

Authorities described the case as unusual. Law enforcement is continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the Instagram-arranged firearm exchange and the fatal shooting.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Resident Maria Jesus Barajas Aguilar Dies
cards.teaser: Maria Jesus Barajas Aguilar of Fort Pierce has died.
cards.body:
Maria Jesus Barajas Aguilar of Fort Pierce has died. Haisley Funeral and Cremation Service in Fort Pierce is handling arrangements.

The funeral home announced the death on Wednesday. Barajas Aguilar was a Fort Pierce resident.

Haisley Funeral and Cremation Service is located in Fort Pierce. The funeral home is coordinating services for the family.

Funeral arrangements are being finalized by the funeral home. The family is working with Haisley Funeral and Cremation Service on memorial plans.

cards.headline: Planned Gun Exchange Led to Fatal Fort Pierce Bicycle Shooting
cards.teaser: A planned gun exchange resulted in a bicycle shooting that killed a teenager in Fort Pierce, according to police.
cards.body:
A teenager riding a bicycle in Fort Pierce was shot and killed during what police say was a planned gun exchange. Fort Pierce police are investigating the fatal shooting.

The shooting occurred after the gun exchange was arranged. The teen was on a bicycle when the fatal incident took place.

Police say the gun exchange was planned prior to the shooting. Investigators are working to determine all the circumstances surrounding the fatal encounter in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Family Honors Late St. Lucie County Firefighter's Birthday
cards.teaser: The family of a late St. Lucie County firefighter held a cookout and balloon release to mark his birthday.
cards.body:
Family members gathered to honor a late St. Lucie County firefighter on his birthday. The family held a cookout and balloon release in his memory.

The event took place Wednesday to commemorate the firefighter's birthday. The St. Lucie County firefighter is being remembered by his family and community.

The family organized the cookout and balloon release as a tribute. The memorial celebration honored the late firefighter's service to St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Motorcyclist Faces Super Speeder Law Penalties
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie motorcyclist is subject to harsher punishment under the Super Speeder law.
cards.body:
A motorcyclist in Port St. Lucie faces harsher penalties under Florida's Super Speeder law. The law imposes stricter punishments for excessive speeding violations.

The Port St. Lucie motorcyclist was cited for a speeding violation that triggers the Super Speeder law. The law applies to drivers who exceed certain speed thresholds.

Under the Super Speeder law, violators face increased fines and potential license suspension. The Port St. Lucie motorcyclist will be subject to these enhanced penalties for the speeding violation.

cards.headline: Man May Be Missing in Fort Pierce During Bicycle Ride to Florida Keys
cards.teaser: A man on a bicycle ride to the Florida Keys may be missing in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
A man who was riding a bicycle to the Florida Keys may be missing in Fort Pierce. Authorities are looking into the man's whereabouts.

The cyclist was traveling through Fort Pierce on his way to the Florida Keys. He has not been located since passing through the area.

The man's bicycle trip to the Florida Keys brought him through Fort Pierce. Authorities are working to determine his current location and condition.

hero.headline: Ixora Park community in Indian River County to receive $1 million federal grant for sewage system upgrade
hero.body:
Congressman Mike Haridopolos announced Wednesday that a $1 million federal grant will help fund a major sewage system upgrade in the Ixora Park community in Indian River County. The Member Community Project Funding is part of a larger $20.8 million initiative to retrofit the sewage infrastructure serving over 230 homes that currently depend on a failing sewer system. This aging system poses a significant risk of contaminating local environmental resources and water supplies.

The Ixora Park community is located adjacent to the County South Relief Canal, which flows directly into the Indian River Lagoon, recognized as one of the most diverse estuaries in the country. According to Keith Drewett of the Clean Water Coalition of Indian River County, the lagoon's environmental condition has deteriorated substantially over the past two decades. "It's dramatically different now from what it was twenty years ago in terms of fishing, swimming. Nobody swims in the lagoon anymore," Drewett said. The organization emphasizes that the upgrade is essential given the area's unique environmental challenges, particularly the high water table and heavy rainfall that causes water to flow underground through the subsurface layer.

The sewage retrofit project will replace aging sewer infrastructure and focus on protecting water quality by reducing the discharge of nitrogen and phosphorus into the Indian River Lagoon. Congressman Haridopolos stressed the importance of the federal investment, stating that it "ensures health and safety to the community by rehabilitating infrastructure for over 230 homes, while also protecting a designated federal resource, the Indian River Lagoon." Beyond environmental protection, the congressman highlighted additional community benefits from the project.

The infrastructure improvements will have economic advantages for local property owners. Haridopolos noted that while replacing sewer systems involves significant costs, the upgrades provide dual benefits. "By replacing those, which aren't cheap, it improves not only the quality of the water, which we all want to be out on the water, but the other part of it, you also improve the taxable value of your home," he said. This combination of environmental restoration and economic improvement positions the sewage system upgrade as an investment in both the community's health and its long-term property values.
